title: Workplace Practices and Work Management
summary: A workplace is an environment where people work to produce a product or provide a service. Workplaces differ in schedule flexibility but none compromises on the deadline or quality of work; a valued employee follows the rules and policies. Workplace practices universally applicable: be punctual (on time earns respect and keeps you aware of updates); be aware of your role and the short- and long-term goals; know the organizational chart (a diagram of the structure of an organization showing reporting hierarchy, workflow and your supervisors and subordinates); communication that is clear, concise and effective with colleagues, superiors, subordinates and customers, using the language rules of the organization; team building (no employee works in isolation; mutual trust and accountability); respect (give respect to earn it; respect privacy, cleanliness and the co-workers' working environment).

Ineffective work management leads to stress, which can lead to anger affecting health and career. Tips: plan (a 'To Do' list, kept updated); prioritize (by urgency and time required; one work at a time); stay updated with technology (mail merge for many letters and labels, Google Docs for collaborative review); take timeout (short breaks reduce stress); follow guidelines (read instructions and formats before starting); communicate (ask seniors and colleagues for help when stuck); be grateful (give credit to colleagues who helped); never boast (work for perfection, recognition is a by-product).

Self awareness, one of the ten life skills promoted by the WHO, is honest knowledge of self: using strengths, acknowledging weaknesses and converting them into strengths. Self management means managing oneself better, including stress and anger. Anger is an outcome of dissatisfaction and an expression of helplessness, shown as an outburst or withdrawal, with serious effects on health, relationships and work. Anger management: be thoughtful (think before you speak); express yourself when in control, in a non-confrontational way; divert your attention (music, a chat, a brisk walk or jog); avoid the blame game; deep breathing lowers stress; seek help if you cannot control anger. When over-stressed, diverting attention to something enjoyable and doing physical activity brings stress down.
q1: What should be your self-management skills whenever you feel overstressed?
Divert your attention to something enjoyable such as music, a chat or a walk, take deep breaths and take a short break.

What do you understand by the term workplace?
An environment where people work to produce a product or provide a service.
Highlight the importance of communication in the workplace.
It connects colleagues, superiors, subordinates and customers; clear, concise and effective communication avoids mistakes and improves teamwork.
Why is team building important at the workplace?
No one works in isolation; teamwork with mutual trust and accountability helps achieve goals efficiently.
Why should you be grateful and never boast at work?
Gratitude gives credit and builds rapport; boasting is avoided because recognition is a by-product of sincere work.
Why is it important to know the organizational chart?
It shows workflow, reporting supervisors and subordinates and gives clarity of communication.
What is meant by 'Follow guidelines' in work management?
Carefully reading instructions and formats before starting work, so there is no delay or wasted work.
How does ineffective work management lead to anger?
It creates stress due to missed deadlines, which when not managed gets converted into anger.

New tools make work faster, e.g. mail merge for 100 letters and labels or Google Docs for collaborative review.
